s: A company is expanding. The company plans to separate its resources into hundreds of different AWS accounts in multiple AWS Regions. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that denies access to any operations outside of specifically designated Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Create IAM roles for each account. Create IAM policies with conditional allow permissions that include only approved Regions for the accounts.
Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create IAM users for each account. Attach a policy to each user to block access to Regions where an account cannot deploy infrastructure.
Launch an AWS Control Tower landing zone. Create OUs and attach SCPs that deny access to run services outside of the approved Regions.
Enable AWS Security Hub in each account. Create controls to specify the Regions where an account can deploy infrastructure.

w.y: Hundreds of accounts need a central guardrail that no one in a member account can override. AWS Control Tower builds on AWS Organizations and applies SCPs to OUs, including its Region deny control, to deny actions outside approved Regions across every account.

o.A: Per-account IAM policies do not scale to hundreds of accounts, and local administrators can change them.
o.B: IAM users per account are long-term credentials, hard to manage, and not a central preventive control.
o.C: Correct: Control Tower with OU-level SCPs or the Region deny control centrally blocks unapproved Regions.
o.D: Security Hub detects and reports findings; it cannot deny API calls.

s: Configure the Region deny control - AWS Control Tower
